bug_semantics: The POST routes /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events accepted a caller-controlled HTTPS MISP base URL, passed it through _validate_misp_url, and then made a server-side request whose response was returned to the caller. The validator rejected a hostname only when the hostname string itself parsed as a private, loopback, link-local, or reserved IP literal; its ValueError branch explicitly accepted every ordinary domain name without DNS resolution. A caller could therefore supply a domain resolving to an internal address and use the server to reach and read an internal MISP endpoint. Both routes were also callable anonymously, increasing exposure, although the unresolved-domain allow decision is the SSRF root cause.
flaw_origin: Commit b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 directly added website/web/convert/convert.py::_validate_misp_url together with both outbound-request routes. In that first implementation, `except ValueError: pass  # it's a domain name — OK` treated syntactic non-IP hostnames as safe without checking their resolved destinations; the same commit added the unauthenticated handlers that consumed the validation result and returned remote response data.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object names author ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com> and committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>; its message is only `add: [misp connection] can connect to a misp instance and select event to import`, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory GHSA-x373-32xc-7gqv / CVE-2026-73160 identifies SSRF in /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events and references direct fix https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/commit/4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512. The advisory says affected and patched versions are formally Unknown, but describes the domain-without-resolution flaw and the DNS-resolution/login fix.

`git log -L :_validate_misp_url:website/web/convert/convert.py b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48` attributes the entire original 19-line validator to b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48, including the ValueError branch `pass  # it's a domain name — OK`. Corresponding `git log -L` queries for fetch_misp_event and misp_search_events attribute both request handlers to that same commit.

`git show b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 -- website/web/convert/convert.py` shows the causal linkage in one direct diff: the validator is added, fetch_misp_event calls it then requests `${misp_url}/events/view/${event_id}` and returns `resp.text`, and misp_search_events calls it then POSTs to `${misp_url}/events/index` and returns parsed event data. Neither new route has @login_required.

Immediate-parent tree verification: `git grep -n -e '_validate_misp_url' -e 'fetch_misp_event' -e 'misp_search_events' 4637cf8255487759ba648cff7e374d7c995468a5 -- website/web/convert/convert.py` produced no matches (exit 1), while the BIC diff adds all three constructs. Thus the vulnerable mechanism is absent from the direct parent rather than merely moved or refactored.

The BIC is a normal one-parent commit (parent 4637cf8255487759ba648cff7e374d7c995468a5), not a merge, release, move, revert, or identifiable squash aggregate. Repository-wide `git log -S'def _validate_misp_url' -- .` finds b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 as the original addition; the later 672ca701b3933d930470a7688c86f979c0900bf8 path rename is not the BIC.

Pre-fix tree verification at 957c56bdc64bfbbf9fafacc9a410dcbf32371cfd finds the still-vulnerable `pass  # it's a domain name — OK` at website/web/conversions/conversions.py:63 and both route decorators at lines 237 and 314 without intervening login decorators. `git show 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512` then adds socket.getaddrinfo-based resolution, requires every result to have ip.is_global, and places @login_required on both affected routes.

Repository tag boundary: `git tag --contains b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48` returns v1.3, v1.4, and v1.5; `git tag --contains 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512` returns only v1.5. Direct tag-tree checks find no affected symbols in v1.2, find the vulnerable domain-accepting line in v1.3 and v1.4, and find socket.getaddrinfo plus login decorators in v1.5. Therefore the observable repository release boundary is first affected v1.3, still affected v1.4, fixed v1.5, notwithstanding the advisory's formally Unknown version fields.

BIC-only AI inspection: `git cat-file -p b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48` contains tree, one parent, identical human-named author/committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>, and the short feature message; there are no trailers or AI/bot markers. No later commit, PR text, branch name, or fix authorship was used for attribution.
reasoning: The lifecycle begins at b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48, not at a later rename or helper refactor: line-history and pickaxe searches show that it first wrote both the unsafe trust decision and the two request/response paths, and its immediate parent's tree contains none of them. The first release tag containing that commit is v1.3; the same vulnerable decision remains in v1.4. The advisory's commit 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512 is a direct one-parent source fix whose parent still has the flaw: it resolves domain names, rejects the URL unless every resulting address is globally routable, and adds authentication to both endpoints. It is included in v1.5, establishing the repository tag boundary even though the advisory does not declare package version ranges. Because b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 is already the smallest direct BIC and its own commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker or trailer, the protocol requires NOT_AI; unrelated same-repository AI markers and all later commits are excluded from that decision.
